title: Marlene Dietrich's birth chart
metaDescription: Marlene Dietrich's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 5.0° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Five of the nine placements whose signs are settled stand in Capricorn — the Sun, Mercury, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 5.0° Capricorn: the first decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Saturn. An earth sign, read here in its first face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 1.7° Capricorn; Venus stands at 20.1° Aquarius; Mars stands at 25.7° Capricorn. The tradition reads a mind that trusts the measured and the checked from Mercury, taste led by wit and proportion from Venus, drive that grinds rather than flares from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Uranus opposition Pluto, 0.8° of separation. Oppositions are read as full-moon geometry — maximum visibility between two needs that share one spine. Behind it, Mercury opposition Neptune at 1.7°, and Venus sextile Uranus at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, three sit in a sign it has an opinion about. Mars in Capricorn at 25.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Capricorn at 20.3° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Capricorn at 17.2° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of these labels is a verdict on a person; they describe how a function is situated, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 earth, 3 air, 1 fire by element and 5 cardinal, 3 mutable, 1 fixed by modality. Earth weights a chart toward the material and the durable — what can be built, kept, and relied on. No settled placement falls in water — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Cancer into Leo during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.3° between one midnight and the next. The hour would decide it; no hour was recorded. The reading keeps the question open rather than flipping a coin dressed as astrology.
